page_title: Observability: Are You Measuring What Actually Matters?

summary.name: Observability: Are You Measuring What Actually Matters?
summary.one_liner: An essay by Honeycomb's Colin Burke arguing that classic observability metrics like uptime and MTTR must be linked to business outcomes such as savings, speed, satisfaction and product success.
use_cases: Building a business case for observability spend
Deciding which metrics beyond uptime to track
Measuring the customer experience of AI agents
Explaining observability value to finance and product stakeholders
Framing downtime cost and engineering capacity recovered
summary.what_it_does: The essay argues that uptime, error rates, MTTR and tool consolidation are foundational but insufficient because they do not show business consequence. It proposes a five-part value framework: savings, stability, speed, satisfaction and product success. It describes how AI and distributed systems make availability alone a poor signal, and gives an example of Fin.ai building a formal SLI in Honeycomb that tracks time to first token, model performance, routing and conversation-level behavior. It closes with questions teams can ask to build a baseline, such as what an hour of downtime cost and how customer experience changed.
notable: Five-part value framework: savings, stability, speed, satisfaction, product success
Argues slow is the new down: degraded experiences can matter more than outages
Fin.ai case study using a custom SLI for an AI customer service agent
Covers stakeholder shifts from CTO to CPO, CISO and CFO
caveats: This is a vendor-authored essay from Honeycomb, so it promotes its own product and approach
Gives no concrete numbers or methodology for measuring the proposed value metrics
